source_name: ПУМБ / FUIB — Прес-центр (bank press centre, news + notifications + 'Преса про нас')
why_relevant: PUMB is one of the most technology-vocal private Ukrainian banks and names its partners (e.g. digital core built with MiddleWare Inc on Corezoid Process Engine; first messenger banking in Ukraine). Three sub-streams — /news, /press, /notifications — give both self-announcements and third-party coverage the bank endorses.

source_name: Credit Agricole Bank Ukraine — Прес-центр / Новини
why_relevant: Oldest foreign bank in Ukraine (since 1993), systemically important per NBU. Publishes IT-sector partnerships (Kyiv IT Cluster agreement; partner bank of 2U Tech Forum) and system/maintenance notices that indirectly reveal platform changes.

source_name: ProCredit Bank Ukraine — Прес-центр / Інфо-Центр
why_relevant: German-group SME-focused bank operating in UA since 2001; group-standardised IT means its announcements reveal group-level vendor stacks landing in Ukraine. Press contact published (ukr.press@procredit-group.com) for confirmation requests.

source_name: АТ «Універсал Банк» — official site (monobank licence holder)
why_relevant: Universal Bank holds the banking licence behind monobank (Fintech Band partnership since 2017, >10m app users). Regulatory-grade disclosures about the monobank project (incl. the dedicated 'Проект monobank' section) are the only formal corporate channel for that ecosystem.

source_name: monobank / Fintech Band — product & partner announcements (app blog, press, Telegram)
why_relevant: monobank announces feature go-lives and partner integrations mostly through founder social channels and product pages rather than formal PR; it is the reference competitor for digital-channel benchmarking and reveals which processing/issuing/AI vendors sit behind Ukraine's largest neobank.

source_name: А-Банк (A-Bank) — official site / about & news
why_relevant: Fast-moving private digital bank (А24 app) with award-winning mobile banking; announces retail/tech partnerships (e.g. co-branded card with Epicentr) and publishes procurement-adjacent notices such as auditor-selection tenders — a rare public-tender signal from a private bank.

source_name: Банк Конкорд (Concord Bank) — historical corporate site and news archive
why_relevant: Concord was an early technology-forward small bank (first among small/medium UA banks to be principal member of Mastercard, Visa and PROSTIR; fintech-sponsor/BaaS role). NOTE: the DGF completed its liquidation on 05.05.2026 — value is now historical/archival for vendor-relationship mapping and for tracking where its fintech clients migrated.

source_name: Interfax-Ukraine — Telecom/IT news wire
why_relevant: Banks distribute technology go-live press releases through the Interfax-Ukraine telecom wire, which timestamps and preserves them even when the bank later removes the item (confirmed case: Raiffeisen HR&Payroll + employee e-cabinet for 6000 staff).

source_name: PaySpace Magazine (psm7.com) — UA fintech/payments trade press
why_relevant: Dedicated UA fintech/payments trade outlet with a banks section, company profiles (per-vendor pages, e.g. /uk/company/payu) and fintech special projects/awards — an efficient snowball hub for discovering vendors and bank-vendor pairings not announced elsewhere.

source_name: Banker.ua — Ukrainian banking-sector analytical portal
why_relevant: Publishes named comparative projects (e.g. 'Український Open Banking: хто з фінустанов реально готовий', 2026 sector-trend reviews) that enumerate which banks implemented which capability — a shortcut to a bank-by-bank technology-maturity map for private banks.

source_name: dev.ua — Ukrainian tech media, banking-IT coverage
why_relevant: Covers bank IT projects from the engineering angle (e.g. AI in banking with Sense Bank as worked example), often naming internal platforms, teams and suppliers that PR copy omits.

source_name: AIN.UA — Ukrainian tech/business media
why_relevant: Covers bank–fintech deals, NBU decisions affecting private banks and product launches; useful corroboration layer and occasional exclusive on vendor selection.

source_name: Minfin.com.ua — per-bank company profiles and news feeds
why_relevant: Aggregates each private bank's news into one stable per-bank feed (universal-bank, procredit-bank, a-bank, concord, aval/Raiffeisen), including items removed from the bank's own site. Also carries registry data (МФО, ЄДРПОУ) for entity resolution across the actor map.

source_name: Finance.ua — per-bank news feeds and bank directory
why_relevant: Second independent aggregator with per-bank news paths for exactly this cell's banks (pumb, a-bank, konkord, credit-agricole-bank, procredit-bank, raiffeisen-bank-aval); useful for redundancy and for detecting quietly deleted bank posts.

source_name: Mind.ua — bank ratings and per-bank news pages
why_relevant: Independent bank-by-bank rating and news pages (e.g. /banks/38-a-bank) with sceptical financial-journalism framing; useful for validating whether a bank's announced 'transformation' is corroborated by third parties.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine — official Telegram channel
why_relevant: Ukrainian banks announce feature go-lives on Telegram before (or instead of) the website; the public web preview (t.me/s/<channel>) is crawlable and carries timestamps, making it an early-warning channel for platform launches.

source_name: FinAwards (Ukrainian banking/fintech awards) — nominations and winners
why_relevant: Award entries force private banks to describe their technology projects publicly ('Best mobile banking app', 'Leading Technologies and Innovations' — A-Bank 2026, Concord 2023, monobank 'Neobank of the Year'). Entry write-ups often name the implementing vendor.

source_name: MiddleWare / Corezoid — vendor case-study channel for PUMB digital core
why_relevant: PUMB's 'digital core' is publicly attributed to MiddleWare Inc on Corezoid Process Engine. Vendor case-study pages are a direct route into the private-bank stack when the bank names the partner only once.

source_name: Ukrinform tag pages for private banks (e.g. /tag-raiffeisen)
why_relevant: National agency tag pages give a persistent, entity-keyed archive per bank — a low-cost way to assemble the full public announcement history of each private bank and to catch partnership signings covered only by the wire.

source_name: NBU (bank.gov.ua) — news and BankID/systemically-important-bank disclosures
why_relevant: Regulator publications indirectly reveal private-bank technology posture: BankID subscriber lists show which banks joined the national identification system and when; systemically-important-bank lists scope the actor map. Not a vendor source, but an authoritative participation register.

source_name: Credit Agricole Ukraine — press service contacts page
why_relevant: Named press-service contacts are the escalation route for confirming an unconfirmed vendor relationship, and the same page pattern (/pres-centr/kontakti) can be replicated across the other private banks to build a press-contact register for the whole cell.

source_name: Асоціація ЄМА — Члени (EMA member directory)
why_relevant: Single richest structured roster of Ukrainian payments actors: international schemes (Visa, Mastercard), ~35 banks, PSPs/fintechs (Platon, NovaPay, EasyPay, iPay.ua, Rozetka Pay, PayForce, Payoneer, FinExpress), plus hardware/services vendors including Printec and GD Next GmbH, and Moldovan banks (Victoria Bank, MAIB). Each logo is an outbound link to the member entity, so the page snowballs into dozens of vendor and competitor domains.

source_name: Асоціація ЄМА — Партнери (EMA partners page)
why_relevant: Maps EMA's institutional network: NBU, Cyber Police, SBU, State Financial Monitoring, plus international bodies (Europol EC3, EAST, Open Banking Europe, Berlin Group), peer associations (АУБ, credit-union and insurance associations), commercial partners (RBR, GD Next, TransferGo, Konsentus, FS Group, Front-U) and payments media (PaySpace Magazine, Fintech Insider, Finance.ua). A one-page partnership graph and a jump-off point to further pointer sources.

source_name: Payments & Security EMA Conference — programme, sponsors and speakers
why_relevant: The annual EMA conference (XXV edition held 23 April 2025) publishes tiered sponsor lists that reveal which vendors are actively selling into Ukrainian banks: Visa as title partner; Bakotech and IIT Distribution as general partners; Tietoevry, OberigIT, Clico Ukraine, Thales, Protectimus as partners. Sponsor tiers are a proxy for vendor commitment and budget; speaker rosters name individual bank/vendor executives.

source_name: Асоціація ЄМА — Бізнесу (Платіжна Рада, Форум безпеки розрахунків і кредитів)
why_relevant: Hub page for EMA's standing bodies — the Payment Council (Платіжна Рада) and the Settlement & Credit Security Forum — whose meeting announcements name participating banks, processors and vendors. Working-group rosters are a finer-grained pointer than the flat member list: they show which actors are engaged in which topic.

source_name: Асоціація ЄМА — новини платіжного ринку / дайджест
why_relevant: EMA runs a recurring payments-market digest ('Новини платіжного ринку від ЄМА', 'Платежі та безпека. Дайджест від ЄМА') that aggregates member announcements, new product launches and vendor deals. Not a directory, but a continuously updated stream that reveals new actors between directory refreshes.

source_name: Українська асоціація фінтех та інноваційних компаній (UAFIC) — Мембери
why_relevant: Member club of Ukraine's fintech association: reported member mix ~66% fintech, 14% IT companies, 14% MFOs, 6% banks. Direct roster of PSPs, lending platforms, insurtech and data companies that rarely surface in bank press releases. Complements EMA (bank/scheme-heavy) with a startup/vendor-heavy view.

source_name: Український каталог фінтех-компаній 2025 (UAFIC annual fintech catalog)
why_relevant: The single most complete enumeration of the Ukrainian fintech ecosystem: the 2025 edition covers 257 fintech companies with segmentation, and is produced by UAFIC with NBU, Ministry of Digital Transformation, IFC, SECO, GGF and Ukrainian Startup Fund support. A yearly, citable, downloadable actor census — ideal seed for an entity master list. The linked URL is a third-party mirror; the canonical copy sits on fintechua.org.
